content: This medication should be stored at room temperature, away from light and moisture. It is important not to store it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the product is expired or no longer needed, it should be discarded properly. This information was last updated in May 2024. Please note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. This medication, commonly known by brand names such as Micronor and Nor-Q-D, is used to prevent pregnancy. It is often referred to as the mini-pill because it does not contain estrogen. While the mini-pill is more effective than certain other birth control methods (e.g., condoms, cervical caps, diaphragms), it is less effective than combination hormone birth control (which contains both estrogen and progestin) because it does not consistently prevent ovulation. It is typically prescribed for women who cannot take estrogen. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. This leaflet contains critical details about when to take the pills and what to do if you miss a dose. Take the medication orally as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. If you experience stomach upset or nausea, taking the pill after your evening meal or at bedtime may help. Alternatively, you can choose a time of day that is easier for you to remember. It is best to begin taking this medication on the first day of your menstrual period. Continue taking one tablet daily without interruption. After finishing the last tablet in a pack, start a new pack the next day without any break or reminder tablets (placebo pills). Your periods may become irregular, heavier, lighter, or you may experience spotting between periods. Missing pills, starting a new pack late, or taking the pill at inconsistent times increases the risk of pregnancy. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on switching from other forms of hormonal birth control to this product. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, bloating, breast tenderness, or weight gain. Vaginal spotting or irregular/missed periods may also occur. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to norethindrone, other progestins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication should not be used during pregnancy and passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., sex hormone-binding globulin, thyroid tests), potentially causing inaccurate results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, refer to the product package for specific instructions. You may need to use backup birth control (e.g., condoms, spermicide) to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly.
